newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woolworths in US, Australia debt issues.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woolworths in US, Australia debt issues.

text.p: Retailer Woolworths Ltd said on Tuesday it had mandated Westpac Banking Corp and AMP Investments to jointly underwrite a A$100 million domestic ten-year note issue.
Woolworths said also it had priced a 10-year US$100 million issue of senior notes to the U.S. traditional Private Placement market.
Woolworths said the U.S. issue was unrated and met with very strong demand from investors allowing the company to accept over subscriptions of US$25 million.

Merrill Lynch & Co and J.P. Morgan Securities Inc co-lead the issue which was priced at 72 basis points above U.S. ten year treasuries, and subsequently swapped back into a mix of Australian dollar fixed and floating rate debt, Woolworths said.

It said investors were being given the choice to select either fixed or floating rate notes with the final composition to be confirmed on the pricing date for the Australian issue. This is expected to occur on or before August 15.
Woolworths said the Australian issue was unrated.

The two issues were Woolworths first into both the domestic and U.S. capital markets and together with the A$800 million five year revolving credit facility finalised in May, completed the company's planned debt restructure, Woolworths said.
It said the committed facilities were completed on attractive terms and with an average maturity of about six years.
